sampling_model.design: One assignment \(X\sim\pi\) is drawn from the finite, positive, predeclared network-exposure fiber \(\Omega\); every bounded-null claim conditions on a row-stochastic \(K\) satisfying \(d_K(A)\geq\pi(A)\) for every nonempty \(A\subseteq\Omega\).
sampling_model.units: The focal units \(U\) and all potential outcomes \(Y\) are fixed finite-population objects.
sampling_model.treatment: Own treatment varies within the fiber while peer exposure is fixed at \(e\) on every legal comparison used by \(T\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every assignment atom has \(\pi(x)>0\); universal validity itself implies \(K(x,x)\geq\pi(x)\), so fibers with atoms heavier than \(\alpha\) cannot reject at level \(\alpha\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no super-population nuisance estimation. Missing potential outcomes are optimized over the finite compatible sharp-schedule class \(\Theta_{r,c}(X,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 proves super-uniformity for conditional randomization tests induced by a finite partition of the assignment space.
Theorem 2 makes arbitrary permutation laws valid by introducing an independent random reference permutation.
Biclique conditioning yields valid exact tests on imputable assignment subsets under general interference.
A power proxy under normality and constant effects guides refinement of biclique decompositions.

Theorem 4 gives an individual confidence set for each fixed effect quantile under exchangeable treatment, while Section 5.5 establishes the simultaneous joint construction over all effect quantiles and threshold exceedance counts.
The paper gives finite-sample improvements for individual-effect distributions and quantiles in completely randomized, stratified randomized, sampling-based, and matched designs.
Theorems 1 and 3 give exact stratified quantile-null tests, a multiple-choice-knapsack computation, and simultaneous inversion.
Theorem 1 establishes asymptotic validity for a class of network heterogeneity randomization tests with adaptive focal assignments.

body.tldr: A finite conditional randomization law need not resample from a partition cell. Universal validity of an arbitrary legal row kernel is characterized exactly by the inequalities \(d_K(A)\geq\pi(A)\), with an equivalent peeling core, an \(O(m2^m)\) separator, and a finite union-of-polyhedra design region. A three-state directed-cycle fiber certifies exact power \(2/3\) for a valid nonpartition kernel versus zero for every legal partition kernel. On a predeclared network-exposure fiber, a row-stochastic kernel satisfying the same subset inequalities yields valid worst-case bounded-null tests; the open mathematical kernel is a terminating formulation for the smallest three-assignment, two-unit shared-schedule pattern and its simultaneous exposure-specific effect-quantile inversion.

project_justification.gap: Conditional randomization under interference is operationally partition-based, while arbitrary-permutation validity relies on auxiliary symmetrization; even the finite-sample distribution and quantile improvements of Chen and Li (2026) remain in complete, stratified, sampling-based, or matched no-interference designs and do not resolve assignment-coupled network schedules.
project_justification.niche: Finite directed legal supports permit overlapping row kernels whose validity and power can be decided before outcomes are observed, while their schedule nuisance remains finite but combinatorially coupled.
project_justification.fill: The project gives the exact row-kernel validity geometry, a worked directed-cycle certificate with a strict partition power gap, and certified power design, then develops exact bounded-null schedule optimization and simultaneous quantile projection on imputable network fibers under the explicit universal-validity inequalities.

body.related_work: Zhang and Zhao (2023) formulate conditional randomization through assignment-space partitions and prove validity by a conditional probability-integral transform; their exact comparator kernel is \(K(x,\cdot)=\pi(\cdot\mid G_x)\), which is strictly contained in the proposed score-uniform row-kernel characterization. Ramdas et al. (2023) validate arbitrary nonuniform permutation laws after a random reference permutation restores exchangeability; that symmetrization informs the contrast with an unmodified deterministic kernel. Puelz et al. (2022) encode imputability through null-exposure graphs and bicliques, which supply legal network fibers and partition kernels. Yanagi and Sei (2022) use an approximate model-based power expression to refine biclique selection, whereas the proposed design problem maximizes exact catalogue rejection probability over the full valid-kernel region and the directed-cycle example proves that the operational partition gap can be strict. Caughey et al. (2023, Theorem 4) give an individual confidence set for each fixed effect quantile under exchangeable complete randomization; their Section 5.5 supplies the joint simultaneous construction, and both are recovered with \(K(x,\cdot)=\pi(\cdot\mid G_x)\) and the predeclared-tie rank score. Su and Li (2024) obtain the multiple-choice knapsack under no interference and a product of independent within-stratum exchangeable complete-randomization laws, recovered by the same partition-conditional kernel on fixed stratumwise treatment-count cells and their within-stratum monotone rank score. Chen and Li (2026) are the closest newer no-interference comparator: their finite-sample distribution and quantile improvements cover completely randomized, stratified randomized, sampling-based, and matched designs, but not a single potential-outcome schedule shared across network assignments. Owusu (2023) addresses nonsharp heterogeneous-effect hypotheses under network interference using adaptive focal sets and asymptotic weighting. Aronow and Samii (2017) provide the exposure-mapping language that defines the fixed-exposure direct effects. The Cai, de Janvry, and Sadoulet (2015) weather-insurance network is the empirical consumer rather than evidence for a theorem.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The universal-validity geometry does not guarantee useful power on every legal support. The directed-cycle witness has \(\Delta_{\mathrm{part}}=2/3\), but singleton inequalities imply \(K(x,x)\geq\pi(x)\), so no assignment atom with \(\pi(x)>\alpha\) can reject at level \(\alpha\). The Cai application must therefore stop if the chosen imputable fiber is too small, if its legal support forces partition kernels, or if its certified partition gap \(\Delta_{\mathrm{part}}\) is zero.
body.honest_scope: The universal iff, recursion, peeling equivalence, polyhedral representation, finite optimizer, strict three-state inclusion witness, certified three-state partition power gap, minimal coupled-pattern claim, and composite-null validity under an explicitly universally valid row-stochastic kernel are theorem claims to be proved. The exact weak-order reduction for the three-assignment, two-unit shared-potential-outcome pattern and the simultaneous projection identity are the first-class open question. The Caughey--Dafoe--Li--Miratrix reduction uses one exchangeable fixed-treatment-count cell, \(K(x,\cdot)=\pi(\cdot\mid G_x)\), a nondecreasing full-sample rank score, and a deterministic tie order fixed independently of assignment; Theorem 4 supplies individual quantile confidence sets and Section 5.5 supplies simultaneity. The Su--Li reduction uses independent within-stratum complete randomization, the same partition-conditional kernel on fixed stratumwise treatment-count cells, nondecreasing within-stratum rank scores, and predeclared deterministic within-stratum tie orders. Chen and Li's 2026 finite-sample improvements for complete, stratified, sampling-based, and matched designs do not settle the assignment-coupled network problem. Cross-exposure simultaneity is outside scope; each exposure is analyzed on a predeclared fiber, and any later combination across exposures requires an explicit level allocation or a new joint schedule theorem.
